page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 shared vCPUs mapped from 8 physical Intel Xeon cores on the x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz and supports hyper-threading with two threads per core. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results place this instance consistently in the average tier for multi-core operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test achieved a score of 21535.52, while the Geekbench multi-core score reached 7768.0. Single-core performance is comparatively weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1124.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 23.39 GB/sec. However, memory bandwidth remains robust, measuring 1518.77 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 107.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

Because the vCPUs are shared rather than dedicated, this instance is highly cost-efficient for workloads that experience variable demand rather than sustained, continuous CPU utilization. The generous 1280 GB NVMe SSD storage bundle provides high-capacity, low-latency local storage without requiring separate block storage attachments, enhancing the overall resource density of the deployment.

This hardware profile is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, where it demonstrates a throughput of 12.01 GB/sec. It is also appropriate for database operations, supported by a Passmark database score of 4649.2 and a Redis SET performance of 23.04 million operations per second. Other viable use cases include software compilation, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and lightweight LLM inference for small models.
description: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a general-purpose Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 shared vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD. While single-core performance is modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1124.0, its multi-core capabilities are solid, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 7768.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 21535.52. The instance offers balanced memory bandwidth, reaching 107.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Given its shared CPU allocation and high storage capacity, this instance provides a cost-efficient platform for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, database operations, and software compilation.
